findings.claim: ENV_FILE="../.env" is resolved relative to the caller's current working directory, so running the script from the repo root writes GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL to the wrong .env file, outside the repo.

verifier.reason: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:5 sets ENV_FILE="../.env" and the script never does a `cd` or resolves against the script's own directory, so the path follows the caller's cwd. Run from the repo root, lines 62-71 silently create or append GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL in the parent directory's .env, outside the repo; it only hits the repo .env when run from scripts/ or another first-level directory.

findings.claim: The script uses the BSD/macOS-only `sed -i '' -E` syntax, which fails on GNU sed (Linux). When it fails, the .env update does not happen but the script still prints that GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL was updated.

verifier.reason: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:68 (patch line 601) runs `sed -i '' -E "s|...|" "$ENV_FILE"`; GNU sed takes the separate `''` as an empty script and the `s|...|` expression as a filename, so it errors and leaves .env unchanged. The script has no `set -e` or exit-status check, so line 73 (patch line 606) still prints "✅ Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL". Determined by reading the code, not by running it.

findings.claim: The deleteCache handler throws a plain Error when the ownership check fails. tRPC therefore returns INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) instead of a TRPCError with NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN.

verifier.reason: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:24-26 throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` when the ownership lookup returns nothing. Nothing remaps it (authedProcedure.ts:26 only adds perf and auth middleware; errorFormatter.ts:25-38 only special-cases ZodError), so tRPC's default wrapping of a non-TRPCError as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) applies.

findings.claim: The handler constructs `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly, which bypasses the CalendarCache.init feature-flag gate and its mock. As a result, cache status and 'Delete cached data' are shown even when the calendar-cache flag is off.

verifier.reason: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:28-29 calls `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly, so the `calendar-cache` flag check in packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.ts:22-28 and the mock's empty-result `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` (calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts:27-30) are never used. With the flag off, any existing CalendarCache rows (e.g. left from when it was on) still yield `cacheUpdatedAt`, so CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:69 shows cache status and 'Delete cached data'; with no rows, nothing is shown.

findings.claim: After the deleteCache mutation in CredentialActionsDropdown succeeds, it only calls onSuccess and does not invalidate viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. Callers that pass no onSuccess, such as EventAdvancedTab, then show a stale cacheUpdatedAt / 'Last updated'.

verifier.reason: The deleteCache mutation at packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:42-50 only shows a toast and calls onSuccess?.(), with no connectedCalendars invalidation (unlike disconnectMutation's onSettled at :61-64). EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372-384 renders SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper without onChanged, so onSuccess is undefined and the connectedCalendars query (refetchOnWindowFocus: false, SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx:152-161) keeps the stale cacheUpdatedAt.

findings.claim: SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) is called with empty data. With updateMany in Prisma 5.4.2 this does not bump @updatedAt, nothing reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, and the call adds an extra UPDATE on every fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache run.

verifier.reason: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1024 calls updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) on every fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache run, and nothing consumes SelectedCalendar.updatedAt (only selected at packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts:899; the UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt via connectedCalendars.handler.ts:31), so the call is wasted work either way. That an empty-data updateMany skips @updatedAt in Prisma 5.4.2 (pinned in yarn.lock) is from my knowledge of the engine, not checkable in this repo, and the engine may short-circuit without emitting an actual SQL UPDATE.

findings.claim: updateManyByCredentialId is called with empty data {} and relies implicitly on Prisma @updatedAt to auto-touch the timestamp, which is unclear to readers.

verifier.reason: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1024 calls `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` with empty data, and the only effect comes from `updatedAt DateTime? @updatedAt` at packages/prisma/schema.prisma:860. The comment at CalendarService.ts:1023 states the intent (touch updatedAt) but not the @updatedAt mechanism, so the clarity concern is real but minor.

findings.claim: The cache 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, which ignores the user's locale (i18n.language from useLocale) and profile timezone.

verifier.reason: packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:89-92 formats the timestamp with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })` and no `timeZone` option, while line 37 destructures only `t` from `useLocale()`. The date is therefore always rendered in US format and in the browser's timezone, not the user's locale or profile timezone.

findings.claim: findUnlockedUserForSession adds updatedAt and googleChannelId to the selectedCalendars select, but nothing reads either field. Every session lookup still fetches them.

verifier.reason: packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts:899-900 adds `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` to the `selectedCalendars` select in `findUnlockedUserForSession`, which runs on every session lookup (packages/trpc/server/middlewares/sessionMiddleware.ts:29). verifier.reason: apps/web/package.json:11 now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` (patch line 10 replaces `ts-node cron-tester.ts`), but no package.json in the repo declares `tsx` and yarn.lock has no `tsx@` entry at all (only `ts-node@npm:^10.9.1` at yarn.lock:44995). npx would therefore have to fetch an unpinned tsx from the registry when the script runs.

findings.claim: When an existing tmole process is reused, the script reads /tmp/tmole.log, which may be stale or missing. This can cause a false failure.

verifier.reason: In the reuse branch, scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:28-31 takes the URL only from /tmp/tmole.log via extract_url_from_log (line 24), with no check that the file exists or belongs to the running process. If tmole was started outside the script, the log is missing or left over from an earlier session, so TUNNEL_URL is empty and lines 56-58 print "Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL" despite a live tunnel (or a stale URL is written to .env).

findings.claim: The migration's auto-generated warning header says the required column is added 'without a default value', but the SQL adds DEFAULT NOW().

verifier.reason: packages/prisma/migrations/20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql:4 keeps the Prisma warning that `updatedAt` is added "without a default value", while line 9 runs `ADD COLUMN "updatedAt" TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`. findings.claim: prisma.credential.findFirst has no select, so it loads the full Credential row, including the key (OAuth tokens), only to check existence and ownership.

verifier.reason: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:17-22 calls prisma.credential.findFirst with only a where clause and no select, so the full row including `key Json` (packages/prisma/schema.prisma:226) is loaded, and the result is used only for the null check at line 24. findings.claim: The migration's DEFAULT NOW() backfills existing CalendarCache rows with the migration time, so 'Last updated' is wrong for those rows until their next refresh.

verifier.reason: packages/prisma/migrations/20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql:9 adds `updatedAt` as NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), so every pre-existing CalendarCache row gets the migration timestamp; packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:173-187 takes max(updatedAt) per credential and CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx shows it as 'Last updated', which stays wrong until the next upsert (repository.ts:150) bumps it via @updatedAt.

findings.claim: The credentialId input validation uses z.number() rather than z.number().int().positive().
